newsitem.title: UK: North Sea, Nigerian differentials stay depressed.
newsitem.headline: North Sea, Nigerian differentials stay depressed.

text.p: North Sea crude differentials stayed at depressed levels on Thursday with Dated Brent trades repeating Wednesday's discounts.
Two Brents for Nov 21-23 loading sold at Dec -48 cents.
"That's obviously where people have decided Brent should trade and I don't think there'll be much change at least for the rest of this week," said a trader
There were no fresh cargoes nominated loading dates on Thursday.
North Sea grades of Ekofisk, Statfjord and Oseberg were also available before the end of November.

Intermonth paper Brent spreads eased to reflect a larger December Brent programme, the equivalent of 48.5 standard cargoes compared to 40.5 for November. "December's looking fairly heavy," said a trader of Brent schedules.
In the Mediterranean, trade houses continued to dominatebusiness amid slack refiner demand.
Traders reported at least one small and two large Urals cargoes being offered for November delivery by trade houses and a further two cargoes were offered out of a French refiner.
However, traders expected few of the cargoes to find homes quickly with most Med refiners covered for November.
"I suspect the refinery offer is just to test the water," one trader said. "He'll probably finish up taking the oil into his own system," he added.
The relaxed physical demand saw differentials to dated Brent staying soft at a value around Dated Brent -80 cents.

West African crudes were also being depressed by slack buying interest and a hangover of November avails, but traders saw some light at the end of the tunnel with Nigeria's decision to reduce December crude export prices seen opening transatlantic arbitrage options early in December.
